function: Learned two-timescale bandwidth allocation for a multibeam GEO satellite: agent 1 assigns beam-level subchannels to beams, agent 2 assigns user-level subchannels to scheduled users (pp. 6-8).
system: GEO satellite at 35,786 km, 19 beams, Ka band, 500 MHz, 220 W, MF-TDMA; 5-15 mobile ground users per beam; no RIS (pp. 3, 9-10).
method: Multiagent PPO (JHRA): beam-level agent on a large timescale, user-level agent on a small one, trained in three stages; reinforcement learning (pp. 6-8).
data_channel: Custom link-budget simulator: Bessel beam gain, FSPL, normal shadowing (TR 38.811 cited), ITU-R P.618 rain, Gauss-Markov mobility; TR 38.821 satellite parameters; no dataset (pp. 4-5, 9).
test_conditions: One simulated GEO scenario (Table II); sweeps of task arrival rate, bandwidth and power; no test of a trained model in unseen conditions is stated (pp. 9-12).
baselines: Non-learned: random allocation (RRA), genetic algorithm (GA); learned: single-agent PPO allocation (SRA) built by the authors, and JHRA variants with other granularities (pp. 9-10).
metrics: Average task delay, delay fairness (max-min of average delay), weighted objective, training iterations to converge (pp. 5, 11-12).
complexity: Complexity orders of the single-agent SRA and of each JHRA agent in beams, subchannels and neurons (Eqs. 23-25); no FLOPs or measured runtime (pp. 8-9).
q1_support: p. 5: "the MBS, which contains shadowing fading, rain fading, and" free-space loss; normal shadowing (TR 38.811 cited) and ITU-R P.618 rain form a custom link budget with a Bessel beam gain (p. 4). No complete standardized channel model or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 11: "increase in the user task arrival rate p, demonstrating the"; sweeps of arrival rate, bandwidth and power (Figs. 7-12) are reported, but the paper never states that a trained model is tested in a setting unseen in training (single scenario in Table II, p. 10).
q3_support: p. 10: "6) GA: In this algorithm, the GAs is utilized to allocate" (non-learned, with random RRA); the only learned baseline is p. 8: "propose a single agent-based resource allocation (SRA) algorithm as a comparative scheme", the authors' single-agent version of JHRA, and no earlier learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 9: "In the context of the JHRA algorithm, the complexity"; Section IV-D (pp. 8-9) gives the complexity order of the SRA algorithm and of each JHRA agent, Eqs. (23)-(25).
q5_support: p. 9: "which has 19 beams. The parameter settings are summarized"; the channel, mobility and task models are simulated from Tables II and III, with no code or data link, no public dataset and no measured data.
notes: Included under the satellite rule that learned bandwidth (resource) allocation is physical layer, so area 6; user scheduling is not learned (probabilistic priority selection, p. 6). q1: shadowing statistics cite TR 38.811 [34], rain attenuation cites ITU-R P.618 [35] and satellite gain and aperture cite TR 38.821 [38] (pp. 5, 9), but the channel is a custom link budget, so 0; the reviewer may judge these standards as met. q3: SRA is the authors' single-agent PPO counterpart that shares the user-priority design of JHRA (p. 8), so it is treated as a variant, an ablation of the hierarchy; the reviewer may count it as a learned baseline. Metrics are delay and fairness, not a radio metric.
